newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares jump, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares jump, further gains expected.

text.p: Slovenian shares jumped 2.74 percent on Wednesday as domestic investors joined foreign buyers in snapping up shares in newly privatised firms.
Traders predicted further long-term rises accompanied by buoyant demand.
"Foreigners are not the only ones active in our market. Domestic investors have also been encouraged to invest more," said Karmen Korbun, a trader at Creditanstalt.
She said that future price rises may not be so steep but she expected the upward trend to last for a while.

Traders welcomed news that the Ljubljana stock exchange will introduce a new blue-chip index early next year to replace the SBI index. The index will be weighted to reflect market capitalisation, bourse president Drasko Veselinovic told Reuters.
"The new index will reflect the situation on the market more realistic," Korbun added.
* The seven-share SBI index rose 31.69 points to 1,186.59.
* 14 shares rose and five fell, while five were untraded.
* Turnover fell to 338.2 million tolars from 433.5 million.
* Drug company Lek's new issue "A" was the most actively traded, firming 0.85 to 19,908 tolars on volume of 4,940 shares for total turnover of 98.3 million tolars.
* Food producer Kolinska was the biggest gainer, firming 9.70 percent to 2,071 tolars on volume of 25,601 shares for total turnover of 53 million tolars.

* Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, falling 9.65 percent to 27,399 tolars on volume of 64 shares for total turnover of 1.8 million tolars. --Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
